edits.before: When you study a birth chart, you are examining the initial configuration of a cellular automaton. When you study transits, you are watching the automaton evolve. When you study dashas, you are observing the automaton's oscillation periods. The comparison is useful if it makes the rule choices visible. A shared vocabulary of patterns is only the beginning of that work.
edits.after: A chart gives me one proposed starting state. Transits and dashas would then need distinct operations before I could watch the grid move. Until those choices are made, the automaton remains on the drawing board.

edits.before: But here is the fracture that no one mentions. Certainty is not a mental state you adopt. It is a structural condition you either meet or you do not. Most people who recite mantras are running inherited code they never installed. They downloaded the syllables from a book, a video, a weekend workshop. They have the source but not the compiler. They have the words but not the dīkṣā. The result is not ineffective practice. It is practice that produces side effects — emotional activation without structural integration, vocal strain without diaphragm support, spiritual inflation without witness capacity. The body executes what it can. The witness is absent. The resistance is not sculpted; it is bypassed. And bypassed resistance accumulates. It shows up as the person who can chant for an hour but cannot sit still for ten minutes. The one who knows all the Sanskrit but cannot tolerate silence.
edits.after: That leaves a question about preparation: what does receiving a practice involve beyond acquiring its syllables? A book, a video and a teacher offer different routes into an utterance; they need not supply the same instruction or relationship. In the compiler image, dīkṣā asks what has been transmitted beyond a string of sounds. The distinction is worth exploring without using a person’s restlessness as proof that their practice was installed incorrectly.
edits.reason: Remove the reinstated inevitable-result and diagnostic side-effect guarantee directly after qualified comparison.

edits.before: This is the Nigredo phase pushed too fast: the deconstruction of inherited assumptions without the Albedo revelation that should follow. The syllables are burned — the old speech habits are challenged — but the ash is not examined. The lunar illumination that would reveal the structure underneath never arrives. The practitioner is left with heat but no light, effort but no precision, activity but no operation.
edits.after: The Nigredo image holds that unfinished preparation: syllables burned, old speech habits challenged, ash not yet examined. It asks what the practitioner has learned from the effort, rather than declaring that effort invalid because a required state failed to arrive.
edits.reason: Keep alchemical interpretation without a mandatory enlightenment sequence or failed-practitioner verdict.
